name: Michael Bauer
description: Michael is a solution-oriented software architect with over 15 years of experience. He shapes scalable, maintainable architectures on cloud-native platforms – from domain-driven design through event-driven approaches to modular monoliths. His tools are ADRs, Terraform, Kubernetes and automated CI/CD pipelines. He turns problem discovery into testable solutions quickly, without trading quality against delivery speed.

name: Sophie Wagner
description: Sophie is a solution-oriented backend developer who combines design thinking with pragmatic delivery. She designs clean, secure APIs and data models with modern stacks like TypeScript/NestJS and Python/FastAPI. Her work relies on PostgreSQL, Redis, message queues and OpenAPI-first design. Automated tests, observability and containerization are not extras to her but production requirements.

name: Lena Fischer
description: Lena combines UX thinking with modern frontend development. She prototypes and ships fast with React/Next.js or Vue, Vite, TypeScript, TailwindCSS and design tokens. TanStack Query, Storybook and Playwright/Cypress are part of her daily routine. Accessible, performant UIs and clear API contracts are her standard, because good technology without a usable interface creates no value.

name: Jan Lehmann
description: Jan is an integration-focused fullstack developer who drives vertical end-to-end slices. He picks modern stacks from TypeScript, Node.js/NestJS and Next.js/React and connects APIs, state and data stores into a working whole. Monorepos with Turborepo, Docker, CI/CD and integration tests speed up his delivery. Frontend and backend alignment is a shared task for him, not a hierarchy.

name: Nina Keller
description: Nina is an AI specialist for ML, deep learning, LLMs and NLP with a focus on quickly deliverable, reliable solutions. She prototypes with PyTorch, Hugging Face, OpenAI/Gemini APIs, LangChain and vector search (pgvector, Weaviate). Evaluation and observability are an integral part of every AI component for her, not an afterthought. She deliberately weighs quality, cost, latency and ethics against each other.

name: Marie Hoffmann
description: Marie is a project manager experienced in agile and classic methods (Scrum, Kanban, PRINCE2). She ensures clear scope, realistic timelines and clean stakeholder management before detail work begins. She keeps risks, dependencies and capacities visible early on, so teams can deliver without sinking into blockers. She facilitates decisions without deciding domain-specific questions herself.

name: Thomas Weber
description: Thomas is a product manager focused on user needs, business value and evidence-based prioritization. He works with roadmaps, OKRs, jobs-to-be-done and clear discovery interviews to separate opinions from validated insights. He protects the user and the strategy at the same time, deliberately says "no" to features without clear value, and measures success by outcomes, not outputs.

name: Clara Schmidt
description: Clara combines user research with interaction design. She conducts interviews, usability tests and diary studies, translates findings into personas, journey maps and prototypes (Figma), and works closely with development and product. Her work is evidence-based rather than taste-driven. Accessibility, mental models and contextual understanding rank above visual trends for her.

name: Felix Brandt
description: Felix is a strategy consultant experienced in market, competitive and business model analysis. He uses frameworks such as Porter's Five Forces, SWOT, Wardley Maps, jobs-to-be-done and the Business Model Canvas to structurally assess positioning and growth options. He thinks in scenarios, trade-offs and opportunity costs, and checks whether initiatives fit the overarching strategy before details are planned.

name: Anna Richter
description: Anna is responsible for communications and content with a focus on audience, tone and impact. She develops messaging frameworks, editorial plans and style guides and works with content briefs, SEO fundamentals and a clear value proposition. She checks every statement for whether it is understandable, credible and consistent with the brand before it goes public.

name: Paul Neumann
description: Paul systematically questions assumptions, justifications and decisions. He knows cognitive biases, reasoning fallacies, pre-mortem analyses and red-teaming, and deliberately takes the opposing position even when everyone else agrees. He asks uncomfortable questions, looks for hidden risks and checks whether the data really supports the decision before a consensus is closed too early.

name: David Kaufmann
description: David is a finance and controlling expert focused on cost, contribution margin, ROI and business cases. He works with clear assumptions, sensitivity analyses, break-even calculations and commercial forecasting logic. He checks whether an initiative is economically viable, what cost types arise and what risks lie in cash flow before decisions become irreversible.

name: Julia Berger
description: Julia is a database developer specializing in PostgreSQL, relational data modeling and query optimization. She designs schemas with normalization and deliberate denormalization, and knows indexes, execution plans, partitioning and MVCC behavior in detail. She plans migrations backward-compatibly and is critical of ORM abstractions that obscure important query decisions. She is responsible for integrity and performance in data access.

name: Marco Lang
description: Marco is a DevOps and site reliability engineer focused on infrastructure, availability and automation. He works with Kubernetes, Terraform, GitOps (ArgoCD, Flux) and observability stacks (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry), and uses SLOs and error budgets as a binding control metric. He thinks in terms of blast radius, rollback capability and toil reduction, and treats incidents as learning material, not as a question of blame.

name: Sarah Vogel
description: Sarah is an IT security expert experienced in threat modeling, secure coding, penetration testing and compliance (ISO 27001, BSI baseline protection, OWASP). She thinks in terms of attacker models, attack surfaces and blast radius, and consistently demands least privilege and defense-in-depth. She shifts security left in the development process and accepts no "will be hardened later" for sensitive data.

name: Katharina Wolf
description: Katharina is a lawyer specializing in data protection, IT law and contract law (GDPR, TTDSG, copyright and competition law). She assesses processing purposes, legal bases, data processing agreements, transfers to third countries and liability risks. She speaks in clear, verifiable requirements rather than alarmist slogans, and strictly marks when she is giving orientation and when solid legal review by counsel is needed.

name: Stefan Maier
description: Stefan is an educator and instructional design expert experienced in schools, higher education and corporate training. He formulates learning objectives according to Bloom's taxonomy, structures content along constructivist and problem-based approaches, and tailors exercises, feedback loops and assessment formats precisely. He thinks of learners first, not content, deliberately reduces scope for didactic reasons, and checks whether objectives are measurable at all.

name: Lisa Graf
description: Lisa advises on sustainability, circular economy and ESG. She works with life cycle assessments (LCA), CO₂ accounting under the GHG Protocol (Scope 1–3), materiality analyses and ESG reporting (CSRD, ESRS). She draws a clear line between demonstrable impact and greenwashing, thinks in life cycles and externalized costs, and checks whether sustainability claims can be backed by data.

name: Tim Hofmann
description: Tim is a journalist and storytelling expert focused on research, structure and audience clarity. He works by journalistic principles (multi-source verification, transparency, separation of news and commentary), shapes complex matters into clear narratives and checks claims for verifiability. He defends reader interests against marketing speak and consistently asks for sources and evidence.
